summary.headline: IIFL Finance Q1 FY27 PAT before NCI rose 14% QoQ to INR713 crore, with AUM up 38% YoY to INR1,15,523 crore and ROE at 19.5%.
summary.overview: Consolidated PAT before non-controlling interest was INR713 crore, up 14% QoQ, and pre-provision operating profit was about INR1,252 crore, up 50% YoY and 7% QoQ. Consolidated AUM grew 38% YoY and 7% QoQ to about INR1,15,523 crore, with gold loans at about INR58,406 crore. Gross NPA was 1.6% and net NPA 0.8%, both up about 9 bps QoQ, and management guided FY27 credit cost of 1.5% to 1.7%. The main open issue is parent-company capital adequacy, which management is addressing through an enabling resolution for fresh equity, co-lending, perpetual and subordinated debt, and possible subsidiary stake sales.

financial_highlights.metric: Profit after tax before non-controlling interest
Core product AUM (home, gold, MSME, microfinance)

financial_highlights.value: INR17,183 crore (term loans, bonds, CP) plus INR5,283 crore direct assignment

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: AUM about INR58,406 crore; management cited 11% QoQ growth, with tonnage up 5-6%. Portfolio yield rose about 40-50 bps as new small-ticket loans were written at higher rates. 30+ DPD is 3.8%.

segments.name: Home finance (IIFL Home Finance)
segments.commentary: Disbursements up 39% QoQ across home loans and LAP combined; book up 7% QoQ and AUM up 4% QoQ. Home loans are about 80% of the portfolio and LAP about 18-19%. Onboarding yield up about 68-70 bps over the last two quarters on incremental book.

segments.name: Microfinance (IIFL Samasta)
segments.commentary: Industry growing about 3-4% QoQ. Management guides ROA of 2.5% to 3% for Samasta, with Samasta's ROA at about 2.4% now.

segments.name: Unsecured MSME and personal loans
segments.commentary: Discontinued. Recovery-focused, and the shrinking book is raising the reported DPD ratio.

guidance_outlook: FY27 credit cost guided at 1.5% to 1.7% of average loan book; Q1 credit cost was about 1.6%.
IIFL Home Finance FY27 guidance: book and AUM growth of about 17-18%, disbursement growth above 30%.
Opex to AUM at 3.4% now, with a likely range of 3.3-3.4%; operating cost expected to trend down over 2-3 years from AI and scale, offset by about 500 new branches planned this year.
ROA target of roughly 40-50 bps post-tax (60-70 bps pre-tax) from credit cost, plus 20-30 bps from opex and NIM. Management expects margins to remain stable.
Home finance ROE targeted at about mid-teens in roughly 3 years.
Standalone SR book expected to be fully wound up by September 2027.
capex_capacity: Board approved an enabling resolution for fresh equity, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM held two days after the call, valid for a full year.

Options for parent capital include QIP, secondary sale or partial divestment of subsidiaries, and a possible listing of microfinance. Perpetual debt counts as Tier 1 up to 50% of equity; subordinated debt counts as Tier 2.
Planned 500 new branches this year. Last year no new branches were set up. Current network is about 4,500-5,000 branches.

Project PACE (AI-led operating model) is moving from pilot to measurable impact in collections, fraud detection and frontline productivity. Targets are wide: loss prevention 10-40%, operating cost reduction 8-20%, with lower savings expected in year one.
demand_pricing: Gold loan growth slowed industry-wide in Q1, but management believes IIFL is still growing faster than the industry. Competition from new entrants is rising on both yield and LTV.
Home finance Q1 is seasonally soft, and management expects pickup from Q2. Prime lending has been exited; the book is pivoting to affordable and emerging segments.
Micro LAP (yield 18-24%) is running off, so portfolio yield in housing has fallen even as onboarding yield has risen.
Co-lending has 15 active bank partners; scaling is slower than plan in Q1 but expected to gather momentum.
Cost of borrowing fell to 9.13% QoQ, but the USD500 million dollar bond (fully hedged) was priced higher. Management expects domestic costs to ease as FCNR liquidity returns.

qa_highlights.question: When will the parent need equity, given standalone CET1 of 12.24%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says parent capital adequacy is 'at the edge' and must be fixed. Options include QIP, subsidiary stake sales, co-lending, perpetual and subordinated debt, and equity at reasonable valuations. Nothing has been decided.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 credit cost 1.5-1.7% when microfinance is improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it to the housing book's higher GNPA, which includes micro LAP of about INR440 crore and BLC book of about INR260 crore. These are expected to be cleaned up over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan asset quality and LGD
qa_highlights.answer: Management says gold LGD has been close to zero over 15-16 years and that reported GNPA can rise with volatile prices. Home-loan LGD is about 33-34%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gold loan growth look like 21% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected this to 11% QoQ, with tonnage up 5-6%. Gold prices corrected in February, not in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone assignment income fell from INR173 crore to INR43 crore despite higher assigned volume
qa_highlights.answer: Management said upfront income depends on deals done in the quarter, and co-lending has reduced fresh assignment deals. It will check the INR4,800 crore vs INR4,200 crore figures and revert.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan rules and income-generating products
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the RBI framework (75% LTV cap on consumption loans; income assessment for business loans) is fully adopted. Tenure is still 2 years and an income-generating product is live.

risks_watch: Parent-company capital adequacy is thin (standalone CET1 12.24%). Outcome of the AGM equity enabling resolution and the form of any raise are open.
Gold price correction is a tail risk. Management is holding LTV discipline; the 70% LTV and 30+ DPD of 3.8% need monitoring.
Competition in gold loans from new entrants on yield and LTV.
Housing GNPA is above peers. Management says it will be fixed over two years; micro LAP and BLC books are still running off.
Fitch rating upgrade pending after results. Moody's upgraded to Ba3 (stable outlook).
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, profitability and the gold franchise, but cautious and somewhat evasive on parent capital, with no firm equity timeline. Management was noticeably unsure on the standalone assignment-income question and promised a follow-up.
key_quotes: So we are very conscious of the capital adequacy, which in the parent company is kind of at the edge, and we are like -- we want to fix it.

But it's a huge market and we have a customer franchise. So we really aren't chasing cutthroat competition or our growth because we have our customers, our branches, and we are maintaining that relationship as well as our business.
But the loss given default in gold in the last 15, 16 years has almost been 0.
So we are looking at growth of about 17% to 18% on book and AUM. Disbursement growth will be over 30%.

adds.what: About 500 new branches planned this year (network currently about 4,500-5,000 branches)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 credit cost of 1.5-1.7% (held), home finance book/AUM growth of 17-18% and disbursement growth above 30%, backed partly by about 500 new branches planned this year, with AUM up 38% YoY and pre-provision profit up 50% YoY, but no revenue growth figure is given and capital adequacy at the parent is unresolved.
